overview: Enterprise AI adoption accelerates with workflow automation, talent development, and open models; firms focus on governance and cost efficiency.
AI providers release tools for production scaling and faster scientific reporting, emphasizing transparency and reproducibility.
The debate over open versus closed AI development intensifies as capabilities expand into high‑risk domains.

top.title: Chatham scales its capital markets expertise with OpenAI
top.summary: Chatham Financial uses Codex and GPT‑5.6 to automate trade validation, cutting processing time from 30 minutes to under 4, and embeds AI across client‑facing tools while maintaining auditability.

top.title: Anthropic invests $100 million to train 10,000 engineers and tackle the enterprise AI talent gap
top.summary: Anthropic launches Claude Frontier Academy, investing $100 million to train 10,000 Frontier Deployed Engineers by 2027, aiming to close the enterprise AI talent gap.

top.title: A model guide for the GPT-6 family
top.summary: OpenAI publishes a guide for GPT‑6 deployment, offering best practices for model selection, prompt design, caching, monitoring, and cost‑effective production workflows.

top.title: Open-sourcing AstaBrief, the fast report-generation model in Asta
top.summary: Hugging Face open‑sources AstaBrief 8B, a lightweight model for generating cited scientific reports, achieving ~3.5× faster generation than proprietary alternatives.

top.title: OpenAI’s Dot agent is enterprise software that can also order your dinner
top.summary: OpenAI introduces Dots, an enterprise‑focused AI agent platform with avatar UI, capable of interacting with desktop apps and cloud tools, initially limited to Pro users.

top.title: These AI Experts Want to Do High-Stakes Research Out in the Open
top.summary: Trillium Labs, founded by former AI researchers, proposes open‑science approach to high‑risk AI research, publishing experiments to enable broader scrutiny and risk mitigation.
